title: Review: Chemistry — Materials; Chemistry — Earth and atmosphere

Questions: C7#x01 (written for the game), C7#q10, C7#x02 (written for the game), C7#q04, C7#q06, C7#q11, C8#q02, C8#q04, C7#q01, C7#q07, C7#x03 (written for the game), C8#x01 (written for the game). assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Mantle
items.clue: The thick layer of mostly solid rock between the crust and the core

items.label: Brittle
items.clue: Breaks or shatters suddenly, without bending first, when hit or bent.

items.label: Thermal insulator
items.clue: A material that lets energy pass through it only very slowly by heating

items.label: Composite
items.clue: A material made by combining two or more materials so that it has properties none of them has alone.

questions.stem: Which list is in order of reactivity, with the most reactive first?

options.text: Carbon, magnesium, iron, copper
Magnesium, iron, copper, carbon
Magnesium, carbon, iron, copper
Copper, iron, carbon, magnesium

questions.explanation: Carbon sits below magnesium and aluminium but above zinc and iron; copper is near the bottom.

questions.stem: In a furnace, zinc oxide and aluminium oxide are each heated strongly with carbon. Which metal is made?

options.text: Zinc, but not aluminium
Aluminium, but not zinc
Both zinc and aluminium
Neither of these metals

questions.explanation: Yes. Zinc is below carbon, so carbon takes the oxygen from zinc oxide. Aluminium is above carbon, so carbon cannot take its oxygen.

questions.stem: Iron is obtained by heating iron oxide with carbon. Why can carbon remove the oxygen from iron oxide?

options.text: Carbon burns, and heat alone frees the iron
Carbon acts as a catalyst and is not used up
Carbon is more reactive than iron is
Carbon melts the iron out of the oxide

questions.explanation: Carbon is above iron in the reactivity series, so it takes the oxygen from iron oxide.

questions.stem: Magnesium reacts very slowly with cold water. Which element reacts faster than magnesium with cold water?

options.text: Iron (Fe)
Carbon (C)
Copper (Cu)
Calcium (Ca)

questions.explanation: Yes. Calcium is above magnesium in the reactivity series, so it reacts faster: it bubbles steadily in cold water.

questions.stem: In a furnace, iron oxide is heated strongly with carbon. What are the products?

options.text: Iron carbonate alone
Iron and oxygen gas
Iron and nothing else
Iron and carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: Yes. Carbon takes the oxygen from the iron oxide: iron oxide + carbon → iron + carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: Which statement about materials is correct?

options.text: Metals are very good heat insulators
A kettle case is too hard to be a polymer
Ceramics are hard but can shatter
Carbon fibre is light and so it is weak

questions.explanation: Yes. Ceramics are hard and stiff, but they are brittle, so a mug or tile can crack or shatter when dropped.

questions.stem: In the Earth's crust, how are most metals found?

options.text: As lumps or veins of the pure metal
Joined to other elements in compounds
Spread evenly through every kind of rock
As liquid metal that rose from the core

questions.explanation: Yes. Most metals are joined to other elements, often oxygen, in compounds. A rock with enough of a metal compound to be worth extracting is called an ore.

questions.stem: Which statement about the Earth's crust is correct?

options.text: It is the thickest layer of the Earth
It floats on a layer of liquid magma
It is hotter than the rock below it
It is a thin layer of solid rock

questions.explanation: Yes. The crust is solid rock, only about 5–70 km thick. Compared with the whole Earth it is as thin as the skin on an apple.

questions.stem: In the reactivity series, where is carbon placed?

options.text: Below gold, at the bottom
Between aluminium and zinc
Above potassium, at the top
Between iron and copper

questions.explanation: Yes. Carbon sits below aluminium and above zinc. Potassium to aluminium are more reactive than carbon; zinc to gold are less reactive.

questions.stem: Lead is less reactive than iron but more reactive than copper. Which statement about getting lead from lead oxide is correct?

options.text: Carbon can extract it, as carbon extracts any metal
Carbon can extract it, as lead is below carbon
Carbon cannot extract it, as carbon is below lead
Carbon cannot extract it, as lead is unreactive

questions.explanation: Yes. Lead is below iron, so it is below carbon too. Carbon is more reactive, so it takes the oxygen: lead oxide + carbon → lead + carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: Copper wires in electrical cables are coated in a polymer such as PVC. Which properties make the polymer suitable?

options.text: Flexible, and it conducts electricity well
Flexible, and a good electrical insulator
Hard and brittle, to resist scratches
Strong, with a very high melting point

questions.explanation: Polymers such as PVC are flexible and do not conduct electricity, so they make wires safe to handle.

options.text: A layer of liquid rock that the crust floats upon
A layer of liquid iron and nickel around the centre
A thin layer of solid rock forming the surface
A thick layer of mostly solid rock that flows slowly

questions.explanation: The mantle is the thick layer between crust and core: mostly solid rock that can flow very slowly.
